title: Restore water flow through a kinked garden hose
instruction: Straighten the kink in the garden hose until the running nozzle delivers a steady stream. Leave both ends connected.
context: A hose can kink while its source and nozzle stay connected. Straightening the bend restores the lumen and flow without disconnecting the system.
setup: Secure both metal hose connections on a 300 × 368 mm stand. Turn on the water. The 24 mm outside-diameter hose starts in a tight kink of roughly 72° and its fixed brass nozzle points into a collector.
scoring: Partial credit 0.5 when flow recovers to 105 mL/s. Full credit requires both grippers at least 70 mm clear of the bend, 163 mL/s for at least 1.2 consecutive seconds, and at least 200 mL of modeled collection in that interval. The fixed couplers stay connected.
reset_notes: Empty the collector, restore the same supply setting and fold the same section beyond its kink point.
fidelity: A three-joint bend transmits gripper contact. A dynamic wall coordinate models local bore collapse and recovery. Modeled discharge depends on the resulting elliptical aperture, and the collector accumulates flow during the hands-clear proof. The pressure setting and wall parameters are nominal. The outlet beyond the active bend is rendered as a smooth curve. See the timed jug protocol for the matching physical measurement.
